messages:
elaine.p: Heads-up — Legal just filed a DSAR saying a customer claims their records (embeddings + traces) persist past the 3y retention window. They want confirmation of deletion and an audit trail. Can eng-sec/infra confirm snapshots/kms and any RBAC changes in the last 4 years? :eyes:

mason.k: Acknowledged. Do we have a ticket/subject id from Legal? need the tenant + timeframe to trace snapshots and backups.

legal-team: Subject: acct-ACME-388; requested erasure for all PII incl. vector embeddings. They attached a timeline that references queries back to 2021. Asking for evidence of deletion or an approved retention exception.

tyler.i: Quick checks: our scheduled nightly snapshots for embeddings live in gcs under gs://redwood-embeds-prod/snapshots/{tenant}. Snapshots are encrypted with KMS key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/embeds/cryptoKey1. I'll start listing snapshots for acct-ACME-388.

ops-bot: deploy-bot noticed a keystore rotation on 2023-11-02 by service-account:infra-lockbox (reason: emergency key rotation).

mason.k: Two things to validate in parallel: 1) snapshot deletion propagation (we have a backfill job that deletes older snapshots, but some stale copies could live in cold storage), 2) KMS key versions — if the key was rotated, older wrapped data may still be recoverable if snapshots weren't purged.

eva.privacy: From privacy side, if we cannot provide proof of deletion within 30 days we need to escalate to DSAR ops and consider a retention exception request with proper legal sign-off. We should avoid blanket exceptions.

thomas.sre: I ran a targeted query across backup metadata: `SELECT name,createdTime,storageClass FROM embeds_snapshots WHERE tenant=\"acct-ACME-388\" ORDER BY createdTime DESC LIMIT 50;` Output snippet:
```
name: snapshots/ACME/2021-10-12T02:14:22
createdTime: 2021-10-12T02:14:22Z
storageClass: COLDLINE
```

There are 3 entries older than retention window that appear to still exist in Coldline. Need confirm if deletion job completed for that tenant.

mason.k: Can infra run the internal deletion-checker job for that tenant? Command: `infractl snapshot verify-delete --tenant acct-ACME-388 --lookback 5y --output brief`

tyler.i: Running now. If it returns any `orphaned` entries we need to kick the purge: `infractl snapshot purge --tenant acct-ACME-388 --force --audit-ticket RED-5691` (requires eng-security + infra approvers).

mason.k: Also check RBAC logs for any service accounts that had restore privileges recently. Audit log query I ran: `resource.type=\"gcs_bucket\" protoPayload.methodName=\"storage.objects.create\" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail: (\"infra-restore@redwood\")` — found two restore actions in 2023-11 by infra-restore@redwood.

elaine.p: That aligns with the keystore rotation notice. Legal, that means there were restore actions around the emergency rotation timeframe — they might have temporarily rehydrated data.

legal-team: Noted. We need a timeline and who authorized restores. If we have evidence that data was restored then purged, that helps. If data persisted, DSAR might require evidence of deletion or a retention exception.

mason.k: On vuln-triage side, I also want to flag CVE-2024-XXXX — a dependency used by our embedding pipeline had an S3 path traversal issue. We ran hotfix 2024-02-01 but need to confirm whether any exploit could have caused unintended retention or copies outside managed snapshots.

thomas.sre: Triage summary: no indicators of exfil around that CVE for ACME tenant per IDS. But we did find one legacy backup job that copies snapshots to a long-term archival project `redwood-legacy-archive` (pre-2022 config). That archive still contains ACME snapshots.

eva.privacy: Archive = problem. If archive copy exists, DSAR erasure requires we purge those archives or provide legal justification for retention exception. Who owns the archive project?

tyler.i: archive project is owned by `platform-archive` team (team email: platform-archive@redwood). I've pinged them. Platform-archive needs to run `archivectl remove --project redwood-legacy-archive --path snapshots/ACME --ticket RED-5691` and confirm artifact purge.

platform-archive (via ops-bot): platform-archive acknowledged and queued removal; ETA 72 hours. Removing will create a signed purge record + retention exception form if needed.

mason.k: Eng-sec checklist for this thread:
- confirm all snapshot entries for acct-ACME-388 are deleted across live GCS + legacy archive (done by infra + platform-archive)
- verify KMS key versions + whether any wrapped keys allow decrypt of archived blobs (crypto team)
- collect RBAC audit logs showing who initiated restores/rotations and whether they had approval
- attach signed purge receipts to DSAR ticket RED-5691

elaine.p: Also add: run the evidence export script `privacy-utils dsar-evidence --ticket RED-5691 --format pdf` once we have receipts. Legal wants a single package.

legal-team: Please include the audit log query strings and the signed purge manifests. If platform-archive needs a retention exception (e.g., legal hold for forensics), we need a formal retention-exception ticket with scope + TTL.

eva.privacy: I'll prepare the retention-exception template in the privacy tracker if platform-archive claims they cannot purge due to legal hold.

mason.k: One more note: if KMS rotated, we should record KMS key versions in the evidence bundle. Command: `gcloud kms keys versions list projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/embeds/cryptoKey1`

thomas.sre: I'll compile the RBAC entries and key versions. Putting a hold on any automated restore jobs for ACME until we finish purge.

elaine.p: Thanks all. Next update in this thread after platform-archive confirms removal or requests retention exception.

ops-bot: ticket RED-5691 updated: platform-archive removal queued (ETA 72h).
